newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian cocoa prices easier, shrugs of NY rally.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian cocoa prices easier, shrugs of NY rally.

text.p: Indonesian cocoa prices were slightly lower on Wednesday with an overnight rally in New York failing to excite the local market, traders said.
Cocoa was quoted at 2,710-2,720 rupiah/kg in Ujung Pandang, capital of the key growing region of South Sulawesi, compared with 2,730-2,740 rupiah a week ago.

"There is some short covering by exporters seeking to meet their contracts, but otherwise the market is generally quiet," one trader said. He said the mid-crop harvest was winding down in some areas while going strong in others, adding that the harvest will come to a close in January.
Other traders said incessant rains in some growing areas were making transportation of cocoa difficult, and were causing the beans to turn mouldy.

"I have been getting a lot of mouldy cocoa which I have turned down because it was higher than the acceptable three percent," one said. "Some of the cocoa have moulds of up to five percent. Each time it rains, it makes my heart stop."
He said the rains were also making it difficult for farmers to sun-dry the beans. "It all boils down to quality. I have to make sure the cocoa meets import conditions in the U.S."
